page.title: Delivery matrix
page.purpose: Answer the operator's first question — which Android targets can I prove right now, what did the last run show, and what is blocking me.

priorities.statement: Every target row shows a probed disposition, never an assumed one.
priorities.notes: A host being Linux does not imply an emulator works. The row reflects what the last probe proved.

priorities.statement: An unavailable target names its missing capability and next action inline.
priorities.notes: 'Unavailable' with no reason forces the operator into the CLI to find out why, which defeats the surface.

priorities.statement: The gate verdict and the release-readiness summary are both visible without navigating.
priorities.notes: Discovering at the end of a green matrix that no Play account exists is the failure this surface exists to prevent.

priorities.statement: Wherever work executes on a remote node, that node is named.
priorities.notes: Bridge-dispatched runs fail differently from local ones, and an unnamed remote failure is indistinguishable from a local one.

priorities.statement: A passing row carries the grade of the evidence that produced it, even while every strategy reports the same grade.
priorities.notes: Android has no pixel-grade path today, so this is uniform. Rendering it anyway is what keeps a future lower-tier strategy from arriving as an invisible downgrade to results that already look green.

elements.name: Target matrix
elements.description: One row per probed target: ramp, device kind, node, disposition, last run.

elements.name: Target disposition
elements.description: The closed-vocabulary disposition for one target row, carrying a text label as well as a status colour.

elements.name: Release gate
elements.description: The fail-closed gate verdict computed from the matrix.

elements.name: Release readiness
elements.description: Summary of the Google readiness ladder, shown as a peer of the gate verdict rather than behind navigation.

elements.name: Executing node
elements.description: The local host or bridge node that executed or would execute the cell.

elements.name: Generate project
elements.description: The primary action when no generated project exists yet.

elements.name: Evidence grade
elements.description: Whether the evidence behind a passing row can gate a release. Every Android strategy is currently semantic, so this reports uniformly — but it is rendered rather than assumed.

states.description: The matrix as the live system reports it.
Target inventory is being probed; no dispositions are asserted yet.
No generated project exists yet. Explains how to generate one rather than showing an empty table.
Targets are listed and at least one is unavailable — the normal working state on a host without the Android SDK, not a degraded one.
Dispositions are from a probe old enough that they may no longer hold; age is shown rather than the data being silently presented as current.
The inventory request failed. The matrix reports the failure rather than rendering an empty or all-unavailable table.
A required cell failed. The gate reads failed and names the contributing cell.
A physical phone is attached to a host node and appears in the matrix as its own row, alongside the emulator targets.

claims.statement: The release gate verdict and the release-readiness summary are both present on the matrix without navigating away.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-010. Validation readiness and release readiness are independent axes. Collapsing them is how a fully passing matrix gets read as ready to ship.

claims.statement: Every verdict on this page is carried by the matrix and its disposition labels, so no recording has to be played to read it.
claims.rationale: Journey video is evidence, not interface.

claims.statement: Every state in which work executes on a node names that node.
claims.rationale: S2A-P1-002. Bridge-dispatched runs fail differently from local ones; an unnamed remote failure is indistinguishable from a local one.

claims.statement: A matrix with unavailable rows renders distinguishably from a fully available one.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-003. A host without the SDK is the normal starting state; it must be readable as such rather than as breakage.

claims.statement: The empty state presents the generate action rather than an empty table.
claims.rationale: An empty table is indistinguishable from a broken probe.

claims.statement: Every disposition is distinguishable without relying on hue — each carries a shape or text label as well as a status colour.
claims.rationale: DESIGN.md accessibility floor. 'unsupported' and 'unavailable' are semantically opposite — terminal versus actionable — and must not depend on colour discrimination to tell apart.

claims.statement: A physical-device row names the host node through which the device is reached.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-003. A phone is a peripheral of a node rather than a fleet member in its own right. When it goes unreachable the operator needs to know which machine to check, and a row without a host cannot say.

claims.statement: Every matrix row that carries a verdict also carries the grade of the evidence behind it.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-010. Evidence grade is a property of a pass. Rendering it while it is uniform is what makes a later non-uniform case visible instead of silent.

claims.statement: Android renders evidence grade on every verdict row despite every current strategy being semantic, and declares no pixel-grade state because none exists on this platform.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-004. The iOS ramp has a real pixel-grade strategy and therefore a state-distinct claim; Android does not, and inventing one would fabricate a state the system cannot enter. This asymmetry is a deliberate decision, not a gap to be closed by adding symmetry.
